title: The bird in the cage
hookLine: a wandering singer with a one-stringed instrument asks where the bird in the cage comes from
carry: the Lord sits in every heart, whatever the caste
tomorrow: why are thousands walking in the rain to one small town?
last: THE GODDESS IS IN EVERY CREATURE.

lines: HOW DOES IT COME AND GO?
cards: One string, one note, over and over.

On a train platform in rural Bengal, or at a village fair, a singer in a patched saffron robe, hair tied up, holds an instrument with a single string stretched over a gourd, plucks it, and starts to sing.
The song is a riddle. There's a strange bird inside the cage, he sings, and I can't tell how it comes and goes. If I could catch it, I'd tie it with the chains of my mind.
Our last day in Bengal: the wandering singers called Bauls.

teach.b: That song, in paraphrase, is Lalon's, a Baul singer remembered for songs like it. The cage is the body. The bird is something living inside it that the singer can feel but can't see or hold.
In songs like this, God isn't looked for mainly in temples or books.
The Bauls sing of the moner manush, the person of the heart: the one you're looking for is already inside you, closer than your own breath, and you keep missing him. That's why the songs are riddles.
You can't point straight at something that close. The Bauls also show where Bengal's streams run into each other.
Some of their songs borrow the love of Radha and Krishna from the Vaishnava stream, and some readers hear Sufi Muslim devotion in them too.
Caste had a first, gentle answer early on this path; here a singer meets it with a riddle.
Lalon, in another song, says, in paraphrase: everyone asks what Lalon's caste is, and Lalon says he's never seen what caste looks like.
Some wear one kind of prayer beads and some another, he sings, and so people say they're different. The singer won't stand inside the lines people draw.
And under the riddle sits a plain Hindu teaching: the Gita says the Lord dwells in the heart of every being.

teach.h: NO CASTE THE SINGER CAN SEE
teach.b: If he sits in every heart, no caste line can tell you where he isn't. Six days in Bengal, and the streams meet in a song.

how: Bauls travel and sing at village fairs, on trains and at gatherings, accompanying themselves on the one-stringed ektara, and their songs, including Lalon's, are sung widely in Bengal.

games.q: what does “bengal's shakta and vaishnava streams” mean?
o: two Bengali sects that never sing each other's songs
Bengal's devotion to Goddess and Krishna, meeting in song
the rivers of Bengal, each sacred to a different god

games.q: the Bauls of Bengal — tap the pairs.

s: in songs like Lalon's, God is looked for mainly in temples and books
they sing of the person of the heart, already inside, closer than breath.
in Lalon's caste song, different prayer beads are what make people call each other different
and he says he's never seen what caste looks like.
Lalon's songs are plain statements, not riddles
he sings riddles, like the bird in the cage, because what's that close is hard to point at.

games.q: a new kid at the temple youth group gets asked, in front of everyone, what caste his family is. he goes quiet. by Lalon's song, what fits?
o: change the subject kindly: the one we're here for sits in his heart, same as ours.
let him answer; it's only small talk.
tell everyone caste is fine to ask about at temple, just not at school.
games.why: Lalon sang that he's never seen what caste looks like. if the Lord sits in every heart, the line doesn't tell you anything about who's inside.

practice: Feel the body, its edges, its weight, the breath moving: that's the cage, and it's a good one.
Now notice what's alive in it that you can't quite point to, the one who's noticing, and don't try to catch it; keep it company, the way you'd sit quietly near a bird so it won't fly off.
If you pray, you can greet God as the person of the heart, closer than the breath.

wordCard.voice: Bengal's Shakta and Vaishnava streams: the Bauls, wandering singers of the person of the heart, where Bengal's streams run together in a song. Today's word.

carryVoice: Take this with you: the Lord sits in every heart, whatever the caste. A bird in the cage, and no lines drawn. Tomorrow we walk west.
